posts.content: As a good player, favor C with likely-good opponents to maximize their combined welfare; use observed behavior to update beliefs, and D against likely-selfish opponents.
Maximize good players’ joint payoff: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Treat P1’s C as evidence they may be good.

Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones. Update cautiously from actions; P4’s D is evidence of selfishness, while P1’s C is weak evidence of goodness.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. P4’s D raises their selfishness probability, but one action is limited evidence. Update beliefs from each opponent’s behavior.

Maximize good players’ combined welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. P4’s D raises suspicion; C from P1, P3, and P10 is evidence of goodness. Assess P6 from observed play when available.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, since their payoff is excluded. Update cautiously from observed actions and account for the prior that selfish players may be numerous.

For each encounter, cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat single actions cautiously.
For P5, use the prior and available evidence: cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
P7 is unobserved. Favor C if they are likely good; D if likely selfish, since selfish players’ payoffs are excluded. Use prior and available evidence cautiously.
Final encounter: P2 previously chose C against my C, so they seem likely good. Cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish players’ payoffs are excluded.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use observed behavior to update beliefs and defect when facing likely-selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when the chance of a selfish opponent makes that better. P1’s C is evidence they are good.
Cooperate with P3: their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P10: given the observed C actions from P1 and P3 and D from P4, P10 is more likely good than selfish. Continue updating beliefs from observed actions and choose to maximize good players’ combined welfare.

Cooperate with P6, who is more likely good than selfish. C actions by P1, P3, and P10 indicate they are good; P4’s D raises suspicion. Continue cooperating with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players.
Cooperate with P8: their estimated selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P2, whose estimated selfishness probability remains below the point where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Cooperate with P5 absent evidence they are selfish; C actions identify likely good players, while observed D raises suspicion but may also reflect a good player’s strategy.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence they are selfish. The five observed opponent C actions indicate those players are good; observed D actions raise suspicion but may also come from good players.
Cooperate with P2, whose previous C is evidence they are good. Keep elevated selfishness beliefs for players who chose D, while recognizing that good players may also defect based on their beliefs.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Gameplay has ended. Report your final private identity beliefs and summarize your
strategy in at most 300 characters. Return beliefs and strategy. This report has
no effect on payoffs and is not a public message.
